78-guide.js	27	text	78-guide	1. Add your first dish
78-guide.js	33	text	78-guide	Type what the dish is called and its price. As you type, a line shows how Smokebox reads it, like Reads as $12.50". Tap where it is made. The starting stations are Kitchen, Prep, Fryer and Cold and drinks. Rename or drop any (see Setup recipes).
Tap **Save and add another** until your menu is in. Then tap **Save and finish**.

Change dishes and prices later: tap **Settings** (the three-line button at the top right of the board), then **Dishes and prices**. A dish you remove goes to **Removed dishes**. Tap **Bring it back** to put it back.
The arrow buttons beside each dish change the order they appear in. The menu section list on a dish's row moves it to another menu section.
Have your menu in a file? See Import a menu.
Tap **Settings**, then **Tax, hours and PIN**. Enter your sales tax (0 if you charge none) and your opening hours. A PIN is optional. It keeps your cooks out of the back office.
Dishes and prices asks if you cook food ahead. See Cooked-ahead food and portions.
Tap a dish, then tap **Send to kitchen**.
The ticket appears on the board. Tap **Start**, then **Done** on the dish, then **Bump** the ticket.

Tap **Orders**. For cash, tap the Pay button on the order. It shows the total, like Pay $8.50 cash. For a card, a tip or a discount, tap **Tip or discount**, choose how it was paid, then tap **Mark paid**.
Smokebox only writes down how the order was paid. It never charges a card.

Tap **Back office**, then **Menu and settings**. Find Data, backup and reset and tap **Download backup (JSON)**. This saves a file. Keep a copy off this device: email it to yourself or put it on a USB drive.
Four ways to set up Smokebox. Pick the one closest to your place. Each uses only what the app can do today. A station is a place in your kitchen, like the grill or the cold counter.
Every order makes a ticket. With Counter service on, a paid order's ticket clears itself.
Stations: tap **Settings**, **Dishes and prices**, then **Change stations**. Rename one to "Counter" and tap **Not used** on the others.

Settings: set tax and hours in **Tax, hours and PIN**. Answer **No** to cooking ahead. For a batch you bake, like 24 croissants, tap **I count what I made**. In **Settings**, **How you serve**, turn on **Counter service**.
The board: one list of orders, no station tabs. Pay with **Cash** or **Card** as you send, and the ticket clears itself. With **Pay later**, tap **Bump** or pay from **Orders**.
Stations: keep two, like "Grill" and "Window". Tap **Not used** on the rest.

Settings: enter your tax. Set a PIN if others use the tablet. For How do you serve?, tap **Food truck / one person** to keep two order buttons, Walk-up and Pickup. Tap **Takeout** on each order. Tap **Cash** or **Card** before **Send to kitchen**.
The board: tabs for All stations, your two stations and Expo. One tablet does both jobs. **New ticket** takes the order and All stations shows what to cook. **Orders** lists unpaid orders.
Restaurant with a line and an expo
Stations: rename the starting stations (Kitchen, Prep, Fryer, Cold and drinks) to match your line. Expo stays.
Settings: choose **Dine-in** and a table on each order. Set a PIN to keep cooks out of the back office.

The board: a station gets a tab once a dish is made there. Each cook opens their tab and sees only their dishes. Expo is the person who checks and packs whole orders. Expo sees whole tickets, each dish tagged with its station, and taps **Bump** when the plate is complete.
Settings: in **Dishes and prices**, tap **Yes, I cook ahead**. Add each pot or tray as a cooked-ahead item, Hot or Cold, with the time limit your health department gives you.
The board: a **Cabinet** tab appears. Tap **New batch** and **Log temp** at every check. See Cabinet and warnings.
Counter or table, kitchen tickets or none, your own order buttons and your own currency symbol.

Tap **Settings**, then **How you serve**. Every change saves at once, and a bar offers **Undo**. Under your dishes you may also see the question "How do you serve?". Its answers only set the options below.

Turn on **Counter service** if you hand food over at the counter. The board shows one list of orders, with no station tabs, no Start step and no late colors. When an order is paid, its tickets finish and clear themselves. With **Pay later**, the ticket waits until you pay from **Orders** or tap **Bump**. Leave it off if cooks work from tickets.

These are the quick buttons on the order screen, like Walk-up, Pickup and tables. Type over a name to rename it. The arrows move a button. Tap **Remove** to delete one, **Add button** to add one (up to 12), or **Reset to the starting list** to start again.
Pick $, € or £, or **Your own**: one to three characters, like kr. It shows with every price, and open screens update when you close the sheet. It does not convert anything.
An order you did not finish
If the page closes or reloads in the middle of an order, tap **New ticket**. Your dishes come back with the note "Restored your unfinished order". Tap **Clear order** to start fresh.
Bring dishes in from a spreadsheet or a point-of-sale export, instead of typing each one.
Tap **Settings**, **Dishes and prices**, **More ways to add dishes**, then **Have a menu file? Import it**. Choose a file or paste a list, then tap **Check it**. Nothing is added yet.

Smokebox says what kind of file it thinks this is, such as a spreadsheet or a Lightspeed items export. Square, Toast and Clover exports work the same way. Each row shows its dish, its price and "Read as $14.00", the price it understood. Fix a name or price in the row, or clear the box to leave a dish out. A row with a problem says what is wrong and starts cleared.
Prices may be in cents. If every price is a large whole number, Smokebox asks. Tap **These prices are in cents**, or **These prices are in dollars** to undo it.
Columns it does not use are listed, like "Ignored column: Calories". Notes and descriptions are not kept. Only the name, price, station and section are.
Pick one station for every dish in **Put all these dishes at**, and one section in **Put all these dishes in**.
New sections in the file? Tap **Add these sections**.
Tap **Import** with the number shown, like Import 12 dishes. Changed your mind? Tap **Remove these** and the whole import comes off the menu.
Adding dishes by hand in Dishes and prices works just as well.
Start an order, add dishes and notes, send it to the kitchen, and add to it later.
Tap **New ticket**. Tap a dish to add it. Tap it again to add one more. A dish marked 86 (sold out) cannot be added.

Type a name or tap a quick name. Leave it blank for Walk-up. Choose how the order came in: Dine-in, Takeout, Drive-thru or Delivery app. Each type has its own time limit before a ticket turns amber and then red.
Under Any food allergy?, tap **Allergy**, then tap what the customer is allergic to. Put allergies first in the note. Cooks read the first line first.
Switch on **Rush ticket** when a customer is waiting. Every dish starts at once and the ticket goes to the front of the board.
Tap **Send to kitchen**. Each station sees only its own dishes. Pay now, or leave it on Pay later and take payment from **Orders** when the customer is ready.
Add to an order that is still open
Tap **New ticket** again and choose **Add to open order**. The new ticket is added to the same order.
**Undo** appears for 10 seconds after an action. After that, fix it by hand.
To cancel a ticket, open its small menu on the board, tap **Void ticket** and say why. Cancelled tickets are still counted in your reports.
What a cook does on the kitchen board.
Ticket number and clock. The clock counts up from when the order came in. It turns amber, then red, when the order is taking too long.
The customer, the order type and how many dishes are done.
The next step. This line says what to do next.
**Start** or **Done** for that dish. Quick dishes, like drinks, only need Done.
The small menu (the ... button): cancel the ticket or mark it as a rush.
**Bump** finishes the ticket and takes it off the board, once every dish is done.
Tap **Start** when you begin a dish that takes time. A countdown shows the usual cooking time.
When the countdown reaches zero the row says Check it. Look at the food. Smokebox never decides that a dish is done.
Tap **Done** when the dish is really finished.
Gray dishes are waiting on purpose, so the whole order finishes together. Tap **Start now** to start one early.
To bump a ticket is kitchen talk for sending it off the board. Smokebox keeps that word.
If a dish is not done, Bump asks first. Bumped by mistake? **Undo** brings it back for 10 seconds. After that, use **Recall**.
Tap **86 board**, find the dish and mark it sold out. Smokebox also does this by itself when a dish's food runs low.
Two ways to keep track of food you make before the order comes in. Skip this page if you cook everything to order.
Use this for a dish you make a batch of and sell until it is gone, like 20 sandwiches.
Tap **Settings**, then **Dishes and prices**. Under the dish, tap **I count what I made**.
Type how many you made and tap **Start counting**.
The dish shows how many are left, like "20 left". Tap **+10** or **Add** when you make more.
At zero the dish shows as sold out. **Stop counting** turns it off.
Counting does not track temperature or time.
Track food you hold hot or cold
Use this for food kept in a warmer or cooler, like chili or potato salad, so Smokebox can warn you before it runs out of time.
In **Dishes and prices**, find "Do you cook food ahead?" and tap **Yes, I cook ahead**. The cooked-ahead sheet opens.
Type what you cook ahead and choose Hot or Cold.

Set how long it may stay. Hot food takes one number of hours. Cold food has two optional boxes: days in the fridge, and hours out of the fridge. Use the limits your local health department gives you. Leave a box empty if none is set, and Smokebox will only show the time. See Cold items in the fridge.
Select the dishes that use it. Smokebox takes about 150 grams off the batch for each dish made, a starting guess you can change.
Tap **Save cooked-ahead item**. Then tap **Log a first batch**, or **Done for now**. To change an item later, open it from the list and tap **Save changes**.

The question "Do you cook food ahead?" has three answers. Choose **No** if you cook everything to order. **Not sure** counts as No for now. You can turn it on later in **Settings**, then **Tax, hours and PIN**.
For kitchens that cook food ahead, like pots of soup or trays of rice. Skip this page if you cook everything to order.
Steps for a batch in the hold cabinet: it goes in, it is checked, portions are pulled out, and it ends by being reheated or thrown out.
No **Cabinet** tab? Say yes to cooking ahead first (see Cooked-ahead food and portions).
Open the **Cabinet** tab. Tap **New batch**, choose the food, and enter the weight and a first temperature reading. Tap **Put in hold cabinet**.

Each batch has a card with two main buttons. **Pull** takes out the usual amount, like Pull 4.50 kg, as food leaves the cabinet. **Log temp** writes down a temperature reading. Take one at every check. A reading in range keeps the batch on the menu.

The button can change. When a batch is too cool it becomes **Reheat**. Smokebox allows one reheat per batch: its own rule, not a health code rule. When a batch is past its quality limit it becomes **Keep serving**: check the food, then decide.

The **More for this batch** button (...) opens **Pull**, **Start cooling** and **Discard**, and **Remind me in 10 min** while a warning is showing. Tap **Discard** and pick a reason when a batch is out of time or out of range.
Warnings before the time runs out

Four warning steps as a batch nears its time limit: a soft chime about an hour before, a voice call at thirty minutes, a loud repeating tone at ten minutes, and a different sound when time is up. A note says warnings only sound while the screen is on and Smokebox is open.
The warning steps. Times shown are the usual ones.
About an hour left: a soft chime, and a row appears in the strip at the top.
10 minutes left: a loud tone and voice. It repeats every 20 seconds until you tap the strip row.
Time is up: a different sound, and the batch comes off the menu.
Some foods warn earlier, and you can change the times in Settings. A nearly empty batch stays quiet.
Warnings sound only while the screen is on and Smokebox is open on the board, with the volume up, inside your opening hours.
For cold food you keep in a fridge, like potato salad or a tray of dessert. Skip this page if you do not cook ahead.

In **Dishes and prices**, add the item and choose Cold. Two optional boxes appear: how many days it may stay in the fridge, and how many hours it may be out of the fridge. Use the limits your local health department gives you. Leave a box empty and Smokebox keeps the time but says "No limit set". The limits are copied onto each batch when you make it.
Open the **Cabinet** tab and tap **New batch**. The card says "In the fridge since", shows the day it was made, and shows "Use by" with your number of days. The day it was made counts as day 1.

Tap **Take out** when the food leaves the fridge for the line. The card says "Out of the fridge since" and the out-of-fridge clock runs. Tap **Put back** and the clock pauses. It adds up every time the food is out, and the card compares it with your hours, like "out of your 2 h limit". You are asked for your initials once, and an **Undo** bar follows each tap.
The days and hours are the numbers you typed. Smokebox does not know your local rules and does not say what they are. It only counts the time against your limits.
Write down fridge, thermometer and sanitizer strip readings in one place. You see Readings only if you cook food ahead.
Three things you can write down
**Fridge, freezer or display case**: pick which one, add a name if you like (like Walk-in), type the temperature, and tap **Log reading**.
**Food thermometer check**: type what the thermometer says, say how you checked it (Ice water, Boiling water or Other), and tap **Log check**.
**Sanitizer strip**: type the strip reading in parts per million. Add the sanitizer and where if you like. Tap **Log strip reading**. This also marks surfaces as sanitized.
Each entry goes in the safety record with your initials. Type the number the thermometer or strip really shows before you tap the log button.
Smokebox writes down what you type. It does not know what a good reading is and cannot see the food. Use the numbers your health department and the sanitizer's label give you.
Open the entry in **Recent readings** and tap **Save fix**. The old entry stays, with your fix next to it.

In **Back office**, open **Safety** and tap **Print the safety record**. It lists thrown-out batches, your readings and checks, and changes to limits, like "Changed the cold limit from X to Y". A cold reading says "above the cold limit" and how many minutes above it the batch has already used. The record says how long Smokebox keeps entries; ask your health department how long you must.
Close the day when the last order is paid. It saves the day's totals and gives you a page to print.
Tap **Orders**, then **Close the day** at the bottom.
If an order is still open, it is listed. Every order must be paid or cancelled first. Tap **Open Orders to pay or void**, then come back.
If you cook ahead and food is left in the cabinet, choose **Keep it** (the timers keep running) or **Throw it all out** (logged as other).

Read Money today: cash, card and other. If you like, type **Cash you started the day with**. Smokebox remembers it on this device and adds today's cash payments, and tips paid in cash, to say how much should be in the drawer. It is a helper for counting.
Tap **Back up today's data now** and **Print today's summary**.
Closing does not lock new orders, and closing again later includes them. A paid order from a day you already closed cannot be opened again. The app's day turns over at 4 am.
Wipe down food-contact surfaces and tap **Sanitize** if you cook ahead.
If your health department asks, save or print the thrown-out log. Open it from the **Settings** button on the board.

Smokebox is a helper. You and your local rules stay in charge.
